data.title: Orwell Diaries 1938-1942
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文简要描述了叙利亚问题以及英国政府在此事上的立场。文章提到，尽管英国政府不情愿，但因戴高乐坚持认为叙利亚仍属法国 mandate，无法签署条约。戴高乐的态度被视为不幸，但由于他是自由法国的领袖，且国际联盟已不存在，法律地位模糊，英国政府无法采取行动。实际上，叙利亚无法获得条约， blame 被推给戴高乐，英国可能试图为自己谋取利益。文章还引用了哈代的《王朝》中的诗句来比喻这种虚伪场面。此外，提到《每日工人》报重新出现，呼吁开辟第二战场、援助苏联以及提高工资，但最后一点与前两点矛盾。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：乔治·奥威尔的日记及其相关背景讨论，包括其生活背景、作品对比以及对现代社会的反思。

不同观点：
• **[thomassmith65]** 提到奥威尔的日记反映了当时德国暴行的公开宣布，并指出人们对这类事件的反应往往受政治风潮的影响，且这种现象在社交媒体时代尤为明显。他强调了对事实的忽视和历史重演的可能性。
• **[vodou]** 和 **[specproc]** 则关注奥威尔日记中的日常生活内容，特别是他对养鸡等家庭事务的记录。他们认为这些内容虽然琐碎，但为日记增添了趣味性，并提供了对奥威尔个人生活的洞察。
• **[perihelions]** 指出奥威尔在二战期间为BBC工作，负责对印度进行文化广播，这与其私人观点存在明显矛盾。他们还对维基百科使用“文化广播”这一委婉语表示不满，认为这是对奥威尔经历的一种掩饰。
• **[HAMSHAMA]** 和 **[ivape]** 表达了对奥威尔其他作品的喜爱，特别是《巴黎伦敦落魄记》和《向加泰罗尼亚致敬》，认为这些作品反映了奥威尔对社会不公的关注。
• **[jongjong]** 对比了奥威尔的《1984》与赫胥黎的《美丽新世界》，认为现代社会更接近《美丽新世界》中的描述，即通过信息和娱乐控制人们的思想，而不是通过《1984》中的直接压迫。
• **[regularization]** 批评奥威尔在红色恐慌期间向英国外交部告发他人的行为，认为这是虚伪的表现，尤其在他自己曾写书谴责类似行为之后。

补充讨论：
• **[kleiba]** 对博客的逆序无限滚动设计提出质疑，认为这种设计不太合理。
• **[submeta]** 则反思了现代数字日记的持久性问题，认为纸质日记可能比电子日记更能长久保存。

争议焦点：
• 奥威尔在二战期间为BBC工作的性质与其私人观点之间的矛盾。
• 奥威尔告发他人的行为是否构成虚伪，特别是在他曾批判类似行为的情况下。
• 现代社会更接近《1984》还是《美丽新世界》的描述，反映了对不同形式社会控制的理解分歧。

44523722.article_content:
There is evidently trouble in Syria. Handout this morning to the effect that – most unfortunately and much against H.M. Government’s will – General de Gaulle is insisting that Syria is still under a French mandate and it is impossible yet to make a treaty, as in the case of Irak. General de Gaulle’s attitude is considered most deplorable, but as he is, after all, the accredited leader of the Free French and the whole legal position is very obscure (the matter should be decided upon by the League of Nations which unfortunately no longer exists) H.M. Government is unable, etc., etc. In other words the Syrians will get no treaty, the blame for this is placed on our puppet de Gaulle, and if possible we shall swipe Syria for ourselves. When I heard this hollow rubbish trotted out by Rushbrooke-Williams [1] this morning and we all had to listen and keep straight faces, there came into my head, I don’t quite know why, the lines from Hardy’s
Dynasts
about the crowning of Napoleon in Rome:
Do not the prelate’s accents falter thin,
His lips with inheld laughter grow deformed,
In blessing one whose aim is but to win
The golden seat that other bums have warmed? [2]
The Daily Worker reappeared today – very mild, but they are urging (a) a second front (b) all help to Russia in the way of arms etc., and (c) a demagogic programme of higher wages all round which would be utterly incompatible with (a) and (b).
[1] Laurence Frederic Rushbrook Williams (1890-1978; CBE, 1923; Orwell sometimes hyphenated his name, as here), had been Professor of Modern Indian History, Allahabad University, 1914-19, and Director of the Indian Central Bureau of Information, 1920-26. He was Director of the BBC’s Eastern Service from 1941 to November 1944. He then joined The Times (to 1955). His attitude to India was enlightened and is well expressed in his India (Oxford Pamphlets on World Affairs, 1940). He also wrote The State of Pakistan, 1962, and The East Pakistan Tragedy, 1972.
[2] In The Dynasts, Napoleon places the crown on his own head in Milan Cathedral, not in Rome (Complete Edition, 1910, 35; Part I, Act I, Scene 6). Orwell discussed The Dynasts in Tribune, 18 September 1942 (CW, XIV< pp. 42-5).

主要讨论点：潮汐能技术的可行性、成本、环境影响及与其它可再生能源的比较

不同观点：
• barbegal：指出潮汐能涡轮机的维护成本高，只有一个涡轮机在六年内无需维护，其他三个需要昂贵的维修。相比之下，即使在苏格兰，潮汐能也比太阳能昂贵。
• davedx：认为潮汐能具有商业可行性，因其能在潮涨潮落时发电，并能弥补太阳能发电不足的时段。但同时也指出潮汐能的地理限制，只有少数国家具备适合的地点，且全球技术潜力仅为海上风电的十分之一。
• sneilan1：担忧提取潮汐能是否会影响地球自转，虽然作为外行人的疑问，但提出了对潜在影响的关注。
• KolibriFly：对潮汐能基础设施的耐用性持谨慎乐观态度，认为如果能证明其耐久性，将 unlock 巨大的未开发能源。
• NotAnOtter：对海洋中增加更多技术设备持保留态度，担忧设备老化、破损及污染问题，虽然认可潮汐能相比石油更好，但对其大规模应用持怀疑态度。
• edarchis：通过对比法国的 Rance 潮汐电站和韩国的更强力电站，指出试点项目的功率较低。
• KaiserPro：强调海洋环境的恶劣，海水腐蚀性和含沙粒的磨蚀性，以及潮汐的高流速对设备的影响。
• ge96：提到了一种新的球形设计，对其性能表示好奇。
• sgt101：通过历史实例，指出潮汐能的长期可行性，提到一座运行了850年的潮汐磨坊至今仍提供电力。
• g42gregory：关注潮汐涡轮机对海洋生物的影响，特别是鱼类、海豚及微小海洋生物，并质疑某些政治团体利用环保努力牟利。
• sparsely：指出潮汐能的独特性，不依赖于太阳辐射或核裂变，具有独特的能源来源。
• standeven：认为潮汐能技术即便可行，也会面临各种障碍，如误导宣传、政府繁文缛节及关税等，并指出当前太阳能、风能和储能已能解决大部分能源需求。
• Cthulhu_：纠正关于潮汐能涡轮机类似于陆上风力涡轮机的观点，指出很多风力涡轮机实际上安装在海上。
• bilsbie：质疑在已有太阳能和风能的情况下，潮汐能是否值得投资。
• worik：提出在新西兰的辩论，担忧潮汐能涡轮机对鱼类洄游和渔业的影响，呼吁需要事实依据而非猜测。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：潮汐能的成本效益、地理限制、对海洋生物的潜在影响以及与其他可再生能源的竞争关系。
• 重要论据：法国和韩国的成功案例、海洋环境的恶劣条件、新的设计概念及历史实例的支持。
• 讨论关系：观点间存在对潮汐能技术的可行性与可持续性的辩论，部分评论关注环境影响及实际应用中的障碍。

data.title: Regarding Prollyferation: Followup to "People Keep Inventing Prolly Trees"
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“Prolly Trees”的平行发明现象及其特性。作者最初描述了Merkle Tree的概念，通过内容定义的分块器对文件进行分块和哈希，递归构建树结构，用于存储数据版本历史并实现去重。文章引发讨论后，作者进一步探讨了多个独立实现的例子，如2016年的rdedup和2007年的Jumbo Store。此外，Noms的联合创始人Aaron Boodman指出，Prolly Trees与Merkle Trees的区别在于其能够存储结构化数据（键值对），并具备B-tree的接口和功能，而不仅仅是处理文件块。这一特性使得Prolly Trees能够支持快速查找、分支和合并等功能，应用于如CRDTs等数据结构中。Dolt数据库即基于Noms的Prolly Trees实现版本控制功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Merkle树的起源、应用及其变种或类似算法

不同观点：
• Syzygies认为Merkle树并非全新发明，自己在比特币之前就有类似想法，并通过参加Stuart Haber的演讲启发，对原有线性链表进行了改进，提出使用树结构来优化时间戳问题。他强调自己对Merkle树的贡献，尽管最初只是一种调侃式的改进，但最终成为了实际贡献。
• HelloNurse则关注Merkle树或类似算法的性能问题，提出是否存在一种算法，能够通过牺牲性能来保证节点大小的最大限制。这表明HelloNurse更关心算法在实际应用中的性能权衡，尤其是固定大小缓冲区的重要性。

补充讨论：
• Syzygies提到自己曾认为比特币是庞氏骗局，显示出对新技术（如比特币）早期发展的怀疑态度，但同时也透露出对比特币后来升值的遗憾。
• Syzygies作为一名纯数学家，虽然远离计算机科学领域，但通过参加计算机科学领域的讨论，成功将自己的数学背景与计算机科学结合，提出基于树结构的解决方案。
• HelloNurse的评论引出了一个实际应用中的重要问题：在某些场景下，算法的最坏情况表现可能比平均情况表现更为关键，尤其是在资源受限的环境中。

争议焦点：
• 对于Merkle树的原创性及其在实际应用中的价值，Syzygies强调了自己的贡献，但同时也承认其贡献是通过一种偶然的、非正式的方式实现的。而HelloNurse则从实用角度出发，提出对类似算法的不同需求和权衡。

总结：
评论中既有对Merkle树历史和个人贡献的回顾，也有对算法性能和实际应用的讨论，反映出不同背景的人对同一技术的多角度思考。

44494813.article_content:
Blog
Last month I published a blog post about
the parallel invention of Prolly Trees
, where I observed the repeated independent invention of a certain type of data structure within a relatively short period of time.
In short, I described the concept of a
Merkle Tree
created by applying a
content-defined chunker
to a file, hashing the chunks, and then recursively reapplying the chunker to the concatenated list of hashes until only a single chunk remained. Each iteration of this process defined a separate row of the tree, with the leaves containing the chunks of the original file. This process allows for storing the version history of a dataset while achieving a high level of data deduplication.
That post kicked off enough conversation and debate that I felt it was worth taking another look at some of my claims. I definitely recommend at least skimming
the original post
before continuing here. I'll wait.
Okay, all caught up? Great. Let's continue.
Even More Parallel Invention
In my previous post, I included every implementation of this concept that I was aware of, but acknowledged that it wouldn't surprise me if there were more.
So given the amount of traction the original post got, it's not at all surprising that people chimed in with other examples that they either knew about or had created themselves:
The creator of
rdedup
pointed out how they independently invented that idea also using recursive content-defined chunking to build a Merkle Tree back in 2016.
compressedgas on HN
brought up
Jumbo Store
, another implementation of nested content defined chunking used for storing files circa 2007, predating
bup
by two years.
A couple of other people mentioned other previous projects that used a content-defined chunker to build Merkle Trees, such as
this proposal to add file chunking to git
. However, that proposal is missing the most important bit, which is the idea that this chunking is applied
recursively
. In fact, the linked proposal by C. Scott Ananian explicitly rejects the idea of applying the process recursively, saying "I propose keeping this only one-level deep: we can only specify chunks, not pieces of files." So I'm not sure that counts.
What are the Properties of a Prolly Tree?
Of all the responses the last post got, the most illuminating came from
Aaron Boodman
, the co-creator of
Noms
and the nomenclator of the term "Prolly Tree". He chimed in to correct the record, both commenting on Hacker News and messaging us on
the DoltHub Discord
(which I've heard is a really cool place for people who people who love data structures) in order to add some important context. He clarified that:
The Noms team was in fact familiar with bup. In fact, they cite bup as an inspiration in their
technical overview
, and felt it was important to give appropriate credit.
The design of Noms' Prolly Trees had an important innovation over Bup's recursively chunked trees, which justified giving a new name to the data structure.
To quote one of Aaron's comments on Hacker News
:
The reason I thought a new name was warranted is that a prolly tree stores structured data (a sorted set of k/v pairs, like a b-tree), not blob data. And it has the same interface and utility as a b-tree. Is it a huge difference? No. A pretty minor adaptation of an existing idea. But still different enough to warrant a different name IMO.
Essentially, Aaron argued that a defining aspect of Prolly Trees is the fact that they can be used to implement key-value maps. In my original post, I said that "a prolly tree is ultimately nothing more than a Merkle Tree built by recursively applying a Content-Defined Chunker, such as with a rolling
hash function." But Aaron opted for a stricter definition: in order to be a Prolly Tree, the chunking process must understand and utilize the structure of the underlying data in order to expose the same interface as a B-tree. Using recursive chunking is necessary, but not sufficient.
While I did discuss this property in the original post, I presented it as an innovation on top of Prolly Trees, a use case rather than a core requirement. But Aaron is right to highlight it, because it's a property that enables use cases beyond any of the prior implementations.
Noms's best and most novel features were the ability to do fast lookups on structured objects, and its Git-inspired diffing, branching, and merging of values. Aaron would go on to create
Replicache
and
Zero
, which use Prolly Trees to build Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs).
I work on
Dolt
, which started its life seven years ago as a fork of Noms. It's
the world's first version controlled database
. And neither the database functionality nor the version control capability would be possible if we were just building on something like bup; the B-tree-like data model that Noms invented is essential for that.
None of this was possible with bup, or the other projects of its era that used content-defined chunking for the purposes of storing large opaque files. Bu

data.title: Batch Mode in the Gemini API: Process More for Less
data.author: xnx
data.article_summary: Gemini API推出了批处理模式（Batch Mode），这是一种新的异步端点，专为高吞吐量、非低延迟任务设计。该模式允许用户提交大型任务，系统将在24小时内返回结果，且费用比同步API低50%。其优点包括成本节约、更高的吞吐量和简化的API调用。用户只需将请求打包成文件提交，即可在任务完成后获取结果。该模式特别适合批量内容生成、模型评估等任务。Google提供了Python SDK示例代码，方便开发者快速上手。批处理模式现已逐步向所有用户开放，未来还将扩展更多功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI批处理模式的竞争与技术实现，特别是Google和OpenAI的批处理API对比，以及使用中的实际问题。

不同观点：
• **tripplyons** 认为OpenAI已有类似的批处理模式（等待24小时可享50%折扣），并对AI价格下降表示欢迎，乐见这一领域的竞争。
• **lopuhin** 更倾向于OpenAI的灵活处理模式（flex processing），因为该模式也提供50%的折扣，且与常规API兼容，适合需要实时反馈的场景，如评估代理。
• **dsjoerg** 提到之前通过BigQuery使用的旧版批处理模式在开发阶段不适用，因为需要更快的迭代周期，而批处理模式的响应时间不可预测，像是回到了“打孔卡时代”。
• **segalord** 批评Google的产品不一致，质疑为何在Vertex和Gemini上有两种不同的批处理模式，且都难以访问。
• **kerisi** 提到遇到空文本响应的常见bug，并提供了一个相关讨论链接。
• **pugio** 详细描述了与Google批处理API文档不清晰、版本不一致相关的问题，并分享了实际操作中的解决方案和错误处理经验。
• **druskacik** 从成本角度比较了OpenAI和Mistral的批处理API，选择了更便宜的Mistral，但看到Google的新模型后重新考虑其选择。
• **nnx** 希望OpenRouter也能支持批处理模式，以便根据价格和响应时间选择最佳的AI服务提供商。
• **dmitry-vsl** 询问是否可以在微调模型上使用批处理模式。
• **tucnak** 希望2.5模型能在Vertex上提供批处理支持，提到之前与BigQuery集成的经验，并指出缓存提示相关的边缘情况问题。
• **anupj** 认为Google的批处理模式是“以更低价格、更慢速度处理大规模任务”的策略，类似于“半价处理，明天见结果”。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Google和OpenAI在批处理模式上的响应时间和适用场景的不同。**lopuhin** 更喜欢OpenAI的灵活处理模式，因其可以在需要实时反馈的场景下工作，**dsjoerg** 则认为不可预测的响应时间在开发阶段是个问题。
• 另一个值得注意的点是文档和技术支持的不足，**pugio** 详细描述了Google API文档不清晰以及版本不一致带来的问题。
• 成本也是一个重要的讨论点，**druskacik** 基于成本选择了Mistral，但新模型的推出让他重新考虑选择。
• **great_psy** 提出了AI泡沫的问题，认为批处理模式可能表明某些GPU资源过剩，宁愿打折使用也不愿闲置。

Batch Mode in the Gemini API: Process more for less
JULY 7, 2025
Lucia Loher
Product Manager

Product Solutions Engineer
Share

Gemini models are now available in Batch Mode
Today, we’re excited to introduce a batch mode in the Gemini API, a new asynchronous endpoint designed specifically for high-throughput, non-latency-critical workloads. The
Gemini API Batch Mode
allows you to submit large jobs, offload the scheduling and processing, and retrieve your results within 24 hours—all at a
50% discount
compared to our synchronous APIs.
Process more for less
Batch Mode is the perfect tool for any task where you have your data ready upfront and don’t need an immediate response. By separating these large jobs from your real-time traffic, you unlock three key benefits:
Cost savings:
Batch jobs are priced at 50% less than the standard rate for a given model
Higher throughput:
Batch Mode has even higher
rate limits
Easy API calls:
No need to manage complex client-side queuing or retry logic. Available results are returned within a 24-hour window.
A simple workflow for large jobs
We’ve designed the API to be simple and intuitive. You package all your requests into a single file, submit it, and retrieve your results once the job is complete. Here are some ways developers are leveraging Batch Mode for tasks today:
Bulk content generation and processing:
Specializing in deep video understanding,
Reforged Labs
uses Gemini 2.5 Pro to analyze and label vast quantities of video ads monthly. Implementing Batch Mode has revolutionized their operations by significantly cutting costs, accelerating client deliverables, and enabling the massive scalability needed for meaningful market insights.
Model evaluations:
Vals AI
benchmarks foundation models on real-world use cases, including legal, finance, tax and healthcare. They’re using Batch Mode to submit large volumes of evaluation queries without being constrained by rate limits.
Get started in just a few lines of code
You can start using Batch Mode today with the Google GenAI Python SDK:
# Create a JSONL that contains these lines:
# {"key": "request_1", "request": {"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Explain how AI works in a few words"}]}]}},
# {"key": "request_2", "request": {"contents": [{"parts": [{"text": "Explain how quantum computing works in a few words"}]}]}}
uploaded_batch_requests = client.files.upload(file="batch_requests.json")
batch_job = client.batches.create(
model="gemini-2.5-flash",
src=uploaded_batch_requests.name,
config={
'display_name': "batch_job-1",
},
)
print(f"Created batch job: {batch_job.name}")
# Wait for up to 24 hours
if batch_job.state.name == 'JOB_STATE_SUCCEEDED':
result_file_name = batch_job.dest.file_name
file_content_bytes = client.files.download(file=result_file_name)
file_content = file_content_bytes.decode('utf-8')
for line in file_content.splitlines():
print(line)

44492014.article_summary: Gemini API推出了批处理模式（Batch Mode），这是一种新的异步端点，专为高吞吐量、非低延迟任务设计。该模式允许用户提交大型任务，系统将在24小时内返回结果，且费用比同步API低50%。其优点包括成本节约、更高的吞吐量和简化的API调用。用户只需将请求打包成文件提交，即可在任务完成后获取结果。该模式特别适合批量内容生成、模型评估等任务。Google提供了Python SDK示例代码，方便开发者快速上手。批处理模式现已逐步向所有用户开放，未来还将扩展更多功能。

不同观点：
